subject: High-load signal dispatch & premier customer update
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15 08:12 PDT
Subject: [ALERT] Elevated request queue + error spike for mediasync-prod

Team —

Monitoring picked up a sustained spike in request queue latency and a rising 500-rate for the mediasync-prod model routing beginning ~07:42 PDT. Current metrics: 99th latency ~1.1s (baseline 220ms), 500s at ~3.2% of requests (normal <0.05%). The cluster shows CPU saturation on a subset of GPUs and an elevated KV cache thrash rate.

I opened a quick diagnostics run and attached the initial timeline (mediasync_incident_timeline.csv). Key asks:
- Grace: can you spin up a private bridge and loop in CS/Support?
- Ava: would recommend an executive note to MediaSync given they’re a premier customer on Dedicated capacity.
- Stephanie: please pull the recent deploys and config changes from the last 6 hours.

I’m preparing a short technical summary for the bridge.

—Marcus
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mediasync_incident_timeline.csv (csv, 12 rows)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15 08:18 PDT
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Elevated request queue + error spike for mediasync-prod

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 08:12 Marcus Lin wrote:
> Monitoring picked up a sustained spike in request queue latency ...

I’ve created a private bridge for this event (link: https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/mediasync-20270615). Bridge ops: Marcus (diagnostics), Stephanie (deploys/configs), me (customer comms/liaison).

Draft status: I can put together a short executive-facing note for the MediaSync ops/leadership contact; recommend we:
- Acknowledge what we know (impact window + scope)
- State immediate mitigation steps we’ve taken (traffic routing, transient scale-up, cache warm)
- Commit to an ETA for full remediation and a follow-up postmortem within 72 hours

Ava — if you’re okay, I’ll send that note and cc Marcus/Stephanie.

—Grace
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: ops@mediasync.io, support@mediasync.io
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15 09:04 PDT
Subject: Short update: Service impact affecting API responses (MediaSync)

Good morning —

I’m Ava Chen, Head of Customer Ops at Redwood. I wanted to reach out with an immediate update because we detected degraded API responses affecting a subset of requests to your production routing. We know you rely on low-latency inference and I want to be transparent about what we know and our commitments.

What happened (brief):
- Starting ~07:42 PDT we observed increased latency and an elevated 500-rate for requests routed to your environment. Impacted requests are concentrated on one Dedicated GPU pool.

What we’ve done so far:
- Routed a portion of your traffic to an alternate pool to reduce queueing.
- Added transient capacity and applied cache-warming to reduce KV lookup thrash.
- Placed the issue on an active incident bridge — our engineers are prioritizing root-cause diagnostics.

Customer impact:
- A subset of API calls may see higher latency or transient 500 responses. We estimate ~5–10% of request volume experienced degraded responses during the peak window.

Commitments:
- Immediate: restore stable routing and reduce error-rate to baseline within the next 2 hours (we’ll update you at 11:00 PDT).
- Follow-up: a postmortem will be shared within 72 hours that includes timeline, root cause, and remediation plan.

Attachments: initial_exec_update.pdf (summary slide)

We’ll post incremental updates to this thread and the bridge. If you prefer an immediate call with leadership, I’m available now and can join the bridge.

Sincerely,
Ava Chen
Head of Customer Ops | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147
From: MediaSync Oncall <support@mediasync.io>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@mediasync.io, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15 09:28 PDT
Subject: Re: Short update: Service impact affecting API responses (MediaSync)

Thanks Ava — appreciate the quick outreach.

We’re seeing intermittent 500s in our staging and two production regions; the impact is visible in our metrics and is causing retries to queue on our side. Ops team is on the bridge. For now, please prioritize restoring low-latency routing for media-sync-heavy endpoints; if there’s an ETA for the 11:00 update we’ll sync on the bridge.

—Samir Khatri
VP Engineering, MediaSync
ops@mediasync.io
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: ops@mediasync.io, support@mediasync.io
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15 12:05 PDT
Subject: RE: Short update: Service impact affecting API responses (MediaSync) — remediation progress and next steps

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 09:28 MediaSync Oncall <support@mediasync.io> wrote:
> Thanks Ava — appreciate the quick outreach.

Quick update from the bridge:
- Error-rate reduced to ~0.15% after traffic reroute and adding two transient GPU nodes. Full rollback to baseline (<=0.05%) in progress.
- Root-cause hypothesis: a configuration interaction between a recent autotuner rollout and a subset of model shards that increased memory churn and KV cache eviction. Stephanie confirmed the autotuner flag change from 03:15 PDT and we’ve rolled that change back to the previous profile.

Next steps and timeline:
- 12:30 PDT: finish cache warm and validate synthetic traffic runs (we’ll post results).
- 14:00 PDT: post an interim technical write-up to the doc link below with timeline and initial notes.
- Within 72 hours: full postmortem with concrete remediation (code fix + regression test + monitoring rule) shared to this thread and via Redwood support portal.

We’ve attached the draft postmortem for your review — feedback welcome, and we’ll incorporate any customer-observed signals.

Attachment: postmortem_draft.md (preview)

—Ava
Head of Customer Ops | Redwood Inference
